title: Decouple weight-metadata validation from tokenizer init to reduce cold-start latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The model ingest pipeline currently validates weight metadata and performs tokenizer initialization in a single synchronous startup path. This inflates cold-start latency for small scale warmups (observed ~420ms median) and causes timeouts for some edge-case shard arrangements. Problem: tokenizer initialization performs file reads and vocabulary reconciliation that are not required to validate weight shard mappings. Proposal: split responsibilities into (1) a lightweight WeightMetadataValidator that verifies shard manifest, checks hash ranges, and establishes shard activation plan, and (2) a LazyTokenizerBootstrap that kicks in asynchronously and only when a request needs tokenizer-specific ops (tokenize/detokenize). Implementation will introduce a WeightMetadataCache with a small on-disk index, an activation fence to mark a model as load-ready for inference without tokenizer, and a feature flag to gate the async tokenizer flow for ramping. The change aims to reduce cold-start p95 by 60-80% in targeted regressions while keeping correctness and allowing graceful degradation for tokenization-heavy endpoints.
updates: 2025-01-08: Ticket created after postmortem on elevated cold-start latencies during a small canary (observed median 420ms). Related to synchronous tokenizer vocab reconciliation blocking model activation.
2025-01-15: Spike completed. Prototype separates validator and tokenizer bootstrap; weight metadata check runs in ~40ms; tokenizer bootstrap takes ~180ms async. Draft design doc added.

2025-01-22: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decision: keep weight validator deterministic and idempotent; tokenizer bootstrap will retry with exponential backoff and expose a warmup metric. Added requirement to preserve KV cache compatibility and kernel selection metadata.

2025-02-02: Implemented WeightMetadataCache (on-disk index) + activation fence. End-to-end unit tests added for corrupt shard header and missing manifest cases. Perf benchmark: cold-start median down to ~120ms when tokenizer init deferred (local perf harness).

2025-02-10: Integration tests discovered race where async tokenizer bootstrap coincided with early requests that call tokenize. Mitigation: add synchronous fallback that triggers a fast tokenizer init path (vocab-only) if request arrives before async completion; documented in design notes.

2025-02-14: PR open for initial runtime changes and feature flag: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/2219. Requesting review from @sophia-chen and @liam-kapoor on fallback semantics and metrics naming.

2025-02-15: Load test on dedicated infra matches expectations; p95 cold-start reduced from 430ms to 150ms for representative model mix. Noted additional follow-up items for telemetry labels and canary rollout plan.
comments: PM (Evan Reed): This looks high-impact for user-facing latency; please keep canary small and document any behavioral changes for SDKs.
Runtime lead (Sophia Chen): Agree with split. Ensure kernel-selection metadata used by dispatcher is available to the validator so routing decisions are unchanged.
Infra (Jorge Alvarez): Watch disk e2e for the on-disk index—we should fall back to in-memory when ephemeral nodes are marked no-persist.

Review (Liam Kapoor): Suggest renaming activation fence to 'load-ready' to avoid confusion with rollout fences; also propose adding a metric 'tokenizer.bootstrap.duration' and 'weightmeta.validate.duration'.
QA (Priya Nair): Added test matrix for mixed-tokenizer models (bpe + sentencepiece) to ensure lazy bootstrap covers all tokenizers.
acceptance_criteria: WeightMetadataValidator runs during model ingest and reliably produces an activation plan without initializing tokenizer.
Model instances with feature flag enabled should reach 'load-ready' state and begin serving non-tokenizer-dependent endpoints with improved cold-start latency.

Async LazyTokenizerBootstrap completes in the background and instruments success/failure metrics; fallback path initializes minimal tokenizer synchronously if a tokenization request is received before async completion.
No regressions in KV cache behavior or kernel-selection routing; existing unit and integration tests pass.
Performance dashboard shows cold-start p95 reduction >=50% for targeted models in the canary pool.
PRs merged and feature flag rollout plan documented in Confluence.
